references.text: The warning that foreigners who approach the tabernacle shall die is connected to this earlier regulation that unauthorized persons who come near shall be put to death.
The foreigner who approaches the sanctuary shall die—this establishes the principle that the people now fear in Numbers 17:28.
Again it is emphasized that foreigners who approach shall die, which explains the people's fear.
The plague that killed 14,700 people is the immediate context for the people's fear of dying.
God's answer to the people's fear: The Levites are to guard the sanctuary so that no unauthorized person approaches and dies.
Nadab and Abihu died when they approached with strange fire—an example of the death penalty for unauthorized approach to the Lord's sanctuary.
At Sinai, the people were warned not to break through to the Lord, for then many of them would die.
The men of Beth-Shemesh were struck down because they looked into the ark of the Lord, and the people asked, 'Who can stand before this holy God?'
